title: Certify v0.15.0: independence-claim round — every "shares no code" sentence in the corpus measured against the files it describes
description: This release corrects a class of documentation defect running through the Certify corpus: public sentences asserting that a checker shares no code with the pipeline that produced its certificate. An independence audit measured each such claim against the files it describes and found thirteen of them false as written across eight deposited papers (Parts B, D, E, H, J, K, L and M), together with two more in Part A's erratum note, which is not a deposited PDF. Each has been replaced by a measured statement: how many of the checker's executable lines also appear in the generator, how long the longest byte-identical run is and what it computes, which routines are identical after systematic renaming, what independence survives, and what a passing check may and may not be read as. Representative figures, each re-derived for this release rather than transcribed: 58 of check_wedge.py's 141 executable lines appear in the private enumeration engine, with a 16-line byte-identical run covering the Poisson-binomial tail program; 212 of check_demag.py's 558 appear in the generator sources, with 31- and 26-line identical runs against newell.py; 247 of zefoz_checker2.py's 541 appear in its engine; check_prof.py shares 88 of 387 executable lines with check_lower.py; and the three Part J checkers share 24, 30 and 9 lines with a private structure-mining tool whose isomorphism test they reproduce routine for routine. No certified value changed, no checker's verification logic changed, and every mathematical result of Parts A through M stands unaltered: of the twelve scripts touched, every edit is to a docstring or comment, and three published SHA-256 manifest lines were updated in step because the files they name were among them — verify_1435.py in its own paper's manifest, and refcert.py and verify_cert.py in the Kelmans certificate regeneration record, where both digests had gone stale and a reader re-hashing the shipped scripts would have been entitled to read the mismatch as tampering. Two independence backstops that did not previously exist were established before this round was written and are stated in the notes: an exact-rational re-derivation of the Part H bracket by an independent route, agreeing at all five shipped certificates, and an external-anchor check for Part M in which all 352 eigenvalue brackets contain the recomputed value. The round does not claim full coverage — roughly 54 independence claims in the corpus remain untested, including every C-language pair — and CORRECTIONS.md records what was deliberately not taken. The deposit is versioned: the v0.14.0 record keeps resolving to the text containing the superseded sentences, and this correction lands as a new version rather than an in-place edit. The Part E record (v0.5.0) predates versioned deposit for that part and cannot be corrected in place; its CORRECTIONS.md entry is the remedy. Computations carried out with Claude (Anthropic), directed by the author.
